question.value: Verify the accretion-burst origin of the G323 maser flare and constrain the burst energy and accreted mass.

evidence.quote:
Maser observations of the MYSO G323

show evidence of a flare, which was presumed to be caused by an accretion burst. This should be verified with IR data.
The objective of this work is to draw conclusions about the nature of the burst from the derived limits for the released energy and the accreted mass.
The ALMA data are from the programme ALMAGAL (2019.1.00195.L) and were retrieved from the ALMA Science Archive (cite: StoehrALMAScienceArchive2014).

The abstract gives a lower burst-energy error of 0.8, while the main text, Table 3 and conclusions give 0.7; the answer key uses the latter.
Table 1 calls the ratio 100 dust-to-gas, whereas Table 2 calls it gas/dust; this convention must be resolved before implementation.
The model tables use different envelope-infall-rate conventions, including a factor 1.33 in the appendix.
The preferred energy uses the Ks fit with FIR-derived bounds rather than a fully specified joint inference.
The ALMA observations were taken during the late burst, so they are not an independent pre-burst structural measurement.
